newsitem.title: CHINA: China to curb imports of old cars to cut pollution.
newsitem.headline: China to curb imports of old cars to cut pollution.

text.p: China's southwestern province of Yunnan has drawn up regulations to reduce pollution by curbing the import and disposal of used cars and machinery from abroad, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
"Pollution has been increasing and has become a major problem in border areas, with an influx of used cars and other machines that are dismantled on this side of the border," Xinhua said.
The new rules would require those importing motor vehicles or machinery for disposal to get approval, and would ban dumping waste in international waters, the agency said.
"Dumping of industrial waste, garbage, oil, acids, alkalis or poisonous liquids in international rivers is strictly prohibited," it said.
Major rivers such as the Salween, Mekong and Red flow out of Yunnan across international borders.

The regulations would require construction firms in border towns to provide new housing projects with waste disposal facilities, it said, adding that garbage could be dumped and buried only at designated sites.
Xinhua did not say when the rules would go into effect.
Yunnan borders Vietnam, Laos and Burma. The province has 20 official ports of entry and more than 80 border crossings.
Imports of foreign garbage have angered China since earlier this year, when it found what it said was hazardous waste in shipments from the United States originally listed as recyclable material.
